text: Spread and rest both use the exact same three-dot syntax, but do opposite jobs — spread expands a collection out, rest gathers values together. Chapter 2 closes with these, since you'll see this syntax on nearly every page of real code.
Spread expands an array's elements out, in place, inside a new array literal. This is the modern way to build a new array that includes an existing one's contents, without mutating the original.

The same syntax works on objects. Spreading an object then overriding one field copies every property first, then applies the override — exactly the pattern frameworks like React expect for state updates.

Rest uses the same three dots but does the opposite job: instead of expanding a collection out, it gathers any number of individual arguments into a single real array. This is how a function accepts an unknown number of arguments.

Rest also shows up inside destructuring — one property pulled out by name, and rest gathering everything else into its own object. The rule: spread expands inside a literal or call, rest gathers inside a parameter list or destructuring.

Spread to expand and copy without mutating, rest to gather multiple values into one array. That closes out Chapter 2. Next up: Chapter 3, asynchronous JavaScript, where every blockchain call actually happens.
